messages:
Maya (AE): Quick: Aurora Financial asked for a focused perf POC next week. Goals: validate p99/p99.9 at sustained 400 qps, verify behavior for short 20-30s microbursts up to 2k qps, quantify cold-start penalty, and give a committed vs burst pricing sketch. They also want HSM/KMS notes.
Priya (Perf Eng): I can run. Proposed matrix:
- Warmup: 8m (mixed sizes: 70% small ~32 tokens, 25% mid ~128, 5% long ~512)
- Steady: 20m @ 400 qps
- Bursts: 3x 25s @ 2k qps spaced 4m apart
- Post-soak: 30m observation
I'll capture p50/p95/p99/p99.9, batch sizes, queue depth, GPU util, KV cache hit, 5xx, and first-byte-time for cold starts.
Priya (Perf Eng): k6 verbs we'll use:```bash
k6 run --vus 250 --duration 20m aurora_400qps.js
# burst (short):
k6 run --vus 1200 --duration 25s aurora_burst_2k.js
```
Priya (Perf Eng): Load scripts sample from input_size_distribution.json so bursts realistically skew small. I'll check reproducibility seeds and push artifacts to GCS.
Jordan (Sales Eng): For pricing I need two headline numbers by EOD Monday:
- Committed: reserved pool (monthly) with 20% burst buffer -> $/1M tokens estimate + monthly commitment range
- On-demand burst: pure pay-as-you-go with modeled cold-starts -> $/1M tokens estimate
I can do a back-of-envelope now: committed ~ $18/1M tokens (assuming 30% utilization), on-demand burst ~ $42/1M tokens (includes provisioning & idle tax). Will refine with Priya's token/sec numbers after test.
Nate (Solutions): Fallback plan: route policy -> redwood-small-q4 (4-bit quant) for <500ms degraded mode. Autoscaler: scale-up threshold queue_depth>60% or p99>600ms for 60s. Also prepare a circuit-breaker to reject excess with 429s instead of queueing when global capacity hits 90%.
security-team: Aurora wants confirmation on HSM latency. We need a short note for their security questionnaire.
Priya (Perf Eng): HSM note: we measure key unwrap at container start; unwrap ~30-80ms depending on HSM; request path uses session keys so per-request impact is negligible. We'll include an isolated bench measuring unwrap time and include in report.
Maya (AE): Acceptance criteria from buyer: steady p99 < 500ms, burst p99 < 1s, <1% errors across test. If steady p99 > 500ms we need an A/B fallback documented.
Nate (Solutions): Runbook snippet (will push full doc):
1) Provision dedicated-pool/aurora-poC (owner: Priya) 90m before test.
2) Start warmup, confirm KV cache warming >50% hit.
3) Run steady-phase and capture traces.
4) Execute bursts; monitor queue depth and 5xx.
5) If p99 > 600ms during steady: trigger fallback to redwood-small-q4 and scale up nodes.
6) If errors >1% during burst: abort bursts, rollout smaller model, notify AE & infra.
infra-bot: Provision request accepted: dedicated-pool/aurora-poc -> allocating 8 GPUs, ETA ~14m :gear:
Priya (Perf Eng): Metrics we'll include in final writeup: csv of raw latencies, consolidated p50/p95/p99/p99.9, error events timeline, avg batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, token/sec and derived $/1M tokens for both committed and on-demand scenarios, cold-start sample traces. Example expected snips (synthetic):
- steady 400 qps: p99 ~ 320ms, p99.9 ~ 610ms, avg_batch=24, cache_hit=68%
- burst 2k qps (short): p99 ~ 980ms, p99.9 ~ 1.8s, error_rate=0.6% (transient rejects)
Jordan (Sales Eng): I'll convert Priya's token/sec into the pricing sheet and show break-even idle time for reserved vs on-demand. Preliminary: reserved starts to make sense above ~9h active/day for their traffic pattern.
Maya (AE): Client prefers Tue 18:00 PST. Folks ok to run then and review Wed 09:30?
Priya (Perf Eng): Yes I can run it. I'll attach k6 scripts, size distribution JSON, and a small analysis notebook after the run.
security-team: I'll draft the HSM/KMS answers and confirm TLS 1.3 + mTLS options and key rotation cadence.
Maya (AE): Thanks all. I sent the SQ to the client. We'll iterate on the runbook if needed. :thumbsup:
